answer: A seat is a sediment trap bolted to a named inlet mouth. Each epoch the holder photographs new silt beside a hand-drawn atlas sheet marking where the channel scoured since last tide. Sorting and depth follow storm history nobody forecasts, so it cannot be pre-generated; a copied page fails the photo. Two seats sharing a trap show identical depths and both get slashed. A thousand fake seats need a thousand real inlets, a thousand traps and crews at each tide; permits, travel and labour scale with identities, which a sybil cannot amortise. A numbered jade pebble sealed in each trap guards it.
